source_text: Verum ut hic quoque quantum muniamur advertas, a loco medicantis locum intellege vulnerantis. Si Christus salvavit universos, Adam quoque universis nocuisse fingatur.
pass_a_gloss: But that you may notice here also by how much we are fortified, from the place of the one healing understand the place of the one wounding. If Christ saved all, let Adam also be invented to have harmed all.

lemmas.lexica: LS vulnus; Blaise sin as wound
LS medicina; Blaise grace as medicine

pass_b_english: To see how strongly we are protected here too, understand the scope of the wounder from the scope of the healer. If Christ saved absolutely everyone, let it also be imagined that Adam harmed absolutely everyone (compare Romans 5:18) (Romans 5:18).

choices.why: Loaded word in Julian's Latin at 2.136; English follows LS/Blaise range without copying NPNF.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

bible_refs.note: From Pass B Scripture tagging; wording follows Julian's Latin, not a modern Bible.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
